interpretation: KHP matches the published overall per-capita level within ~6% (2.12M vs 2.26M KRW) but UNDER-captures the senior cost concentration (ratio 1.61 vs 2.44). This does not threaten the equity finding: the prediction target is a WITHIN-YEAR TOP-DECILE RANK, invariant to any monotone within-group level shift, so uniform survey under-reporting cannot create the measured over-targeting. Only cross-person rank-distorting differential error could, and cross-year rank stability (Spearman cost_t vs cost_t+1 = 0.48-0.60 within the exposed groups) bounds it. Moreover, the survey if anything UNDER-states senior cost, so the model over-prediction of seniors is a conservative lower bound, not an inflated artifact.
